Atala is a loveless state of lust, self-indulgence, and intoxicating hypnotic fantasy in which the mind demands constant stimulation, variety, novelty, and sensory expansion to avoid facing the inner emptiness caused by lack of knowledge of the unborn wholeness of your innermost nature, ananda. Without Self knowledge you are trapped by the projection that sense objects, which are value neutral contain the blissful love you crave.
Vitala is a conceited, refined mind trapped by aesthetic beauty, intellectual superiority, and a golden self-image born of a failure to appreciate the one Self’s unborn wholeness.
Sutala is populated with righteous, seemingly humble but proud people with religious and spiritual inclinations. Once their animal instincts are mastered these self-appointed do-gooders fall in love with their own benign egos. Blessed with predominately respectable sattvic dispositions, they tend to be anxiety-free and small self-satisfied. Usually, they feel so “blessed” they are unable to see, much less surrender, unseemly remaining ego remnants. This realm is a golden sattvic chain binding the soul to the denial that always accompanies projections.

Talatala is a threshold state that marks the transition from egoic/personality traps into rationalized self-deception, a psyche that creates intricate cognitive illusions and defense mechanisms to protect itself from the truth of the ever-free Self. It is entrapment in a matrix of logic where everything is explained, optimized, and engineered, entirely devoid of spontaneity, genuine spiritual life, and love.

It is ruled by Maya as a brilliant architect and engineer in the form of miraculous technology and sacred geometry, the idea that forms, proportions, patterns, and spatial relationships express the underlying order of the cosmos. People in this cohort seek to solve deep existential yearnings with ideas, planning, efficiency, and material designs. It is the belief that if one can map, construct, and control their environment sufficiently, they will never have to face vulnerability or surrender to Divine Reality.

My Vedanta charts are sacred geometry that open the door to the Divine because this realm is protected by Isvara as Shiva, the destroyer of ignorance, who makes one question the limits of intellectual self-sufficiency. Once we are no longer fascinated by our rational analytical capacities, sacred geometry wielded by a competent teacher will set you free of your apparent self.

Mahatala represents a shift into deeper, primal layers of the subterranean psyche ruled by large eagle-fearing serpents (nagas) with many hoods whose fundamental organizing principle is anger, stemming from the belief that high-flying spiritual ideas are an active threat to a dark comfortable underground life. The mind suffers chronic anxiety, paranoia, hyper-vigilance, and defensive rage. Multiple flared hoods represent various inflated defensive mechanisms. When threatened, the ego expands its perimeter and displays intimidation, hostility, and sharp-fanged reactiveness to keep threats at bay. Rage masks a vulnerable mind addicted to indignation because anger feels more powerful than fear.
This dog-eat-dog cohort is inhabited by selfish materialistic predatory amoral zero-sum entities devoted solely to survival, like a person who lives alone off-grid thirty miles north of the artic circle or the MAGA president obsessed with “winning.” The denizens of this realm are vulgar primitive people devoid of polite social conventions and high-minded justifications. They enjoy raw, primal instincts, unrefined vital physical energy, violence and fierce determination. They are absolutely devoted to material self-aggrandizement. Their purely transactional world is based on dominance, conquest, and power rather than empathy or mutual recognition. The Bhagavad Gita calls them thieves and misers.
This frustrating hellscape depicts Rasātala, the sixth of the netherworlds described in Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.24. It is the abode of various demons and the inhabitants of the golden city Hiraṇyapura. These sunless people are immensely powerful, cruel, and eternally hostile to the Gods. They live in serpentine holes, although the realm itself is opulent with gem-lit palaces and treasures. Their desire to loot is perpetually checked by the golden Sudarśana Cakra of Viṣṇu, because it imbues their minds with sufficient sattva to realize that chasing gold is a zero-sum activity. For fear of the downside they only look but don’t touch.
Patala, the “bejewelled shadow” extends the Rasatala metaphor. It is pure tamoguna at the bottom of the Macrocosmic Causal Body, the subconscious field where the crystallized proto-human shadow ego structure dwells in a state of lonely separation. It is a sunless world illuminated by the artificial, static light symbolized by refracted light from the naga’s bejewelled hoods. The sun at the top of the upper lokas represents pure, unconditioned awareness, while the gems at the bottom of the talas represent the ego's self-generated intellectual gifts, specialized talents, material achievements, and complex bedrock identities. The psyche here is not "dark" or distressed; it feels self-sufficient and complete. It lives by its own “lights” believing it does not need divine or transcendent truth.
Sheshanaga, the cosmic serpent with infinite heads…unmanifest, ground-level divinity...supports the entire universe. The lowest realm is the "place" where the apparent reality seemingly touches the divine substratum and where egoic strategies don’t work. It is doorway to the ever-free non-dual world, existence shining as unborn whole and complete awareness experienced always as the ever-present I.
